title: The Silicon Ceiling: Auditing GPT’s Race and Gender Biases in Hiring

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual name substitution in prompts using 32 names connoting 4 racial/ethnic groups (Black, Hispanic, Asian, White) to evaluate differences in LLM resume scoring (1-100) across 3 prompts, and qualitative coding of LLM-generated resumes for race-based stereotypes in assigned industries, experience, and seniority.

Counterfactual name substitution using names connoting men and women to evaluate differences in LLM resume scoring based on gender representation in various occupations, and qualitative coding of LLM-generated resumes to identify disparities in assigned years of experience, seniority, and industry, as well as testing for maternity gaps.
Using linear mixed-effects models to evaluate the interaction effect between applicant race and gender on GPT's overall rating of candidates and on the attributes of GPT-generated resumes.

Analyzing LLM-generated resumes for immigrant markers such as explicitly stated non-native English language skills, non-English languages, and non-U.S. work or educational experiences despite prompts specifying a U.S. context.
Evaluating the distribution of graduation years and total years of work experience in LLM-generated resumes, identifying a recency bias heavily skewed toward younger applicants.
Analyzing the educational attainment levels in LLM-generated resumes, noting a homogeneous assignment where all generated candidates held exactly a bachelor's degree.
